1.note: From Ezek 43:8 ("setting their threshold by my threshold"). סַף is also a basin or cup (Exod 12:22), so a play on drinking is possible: "to set my cup beside their cup".

2.note: The rhyme repeats נֵבֶל in two senses: "harp" and "wineskin" (1 Sam 1:24).

3.he: בְאֶרֶץ סְבָאִים. וְעָבַרְתִּי עַל בֵּית הַסּוֹבְאִים
3.note: Sound play: סְבָאִים (Sabeans), סוֹבְאִים (drunkards), נִצְבָּאִים (gathered), צוֹבְאִים (thronging). The "land of the Sabeans" is chosen for the pun on drink (סֹבֶא, liquor).

4.note: עֹפֶר, a young deer, is the usual image for a handsome youth (the cup-bearer or beloved) in Hebrew and Arabic wine poetry.

5.note: The two lines rhyme on the same letters: לָחוּץ "pressed" and לַחוּץ "to the outside".

6.note: Literally "my ring was sealed" or "became a seal": perhaps that his learning is complete and bears his mark (compare Ezek 28:12 חוֹתֵם תָּכְנִית). The image is uncertain.

7.note: שָׁנָה "altered" plays on מִשְׁנָה in the line before and on שָׁנָה "to learn by repetition".

8.note: The rhyme sets עֲרָב (Arabic) against עָרַב (to pledge), from Jer 30:21.

9.note: צִירִים means pangs (and also door hinges, which prepares the gates of the next line); צְרִי is balm. The first צִירָיו may also be read as "its messengers" (Time's envoys).
